scenario.description: AWS CloudTrail records every API call in your account. Metric filters can watch CloudTrail logs and trigger CloudWatch alarms on specific events — for example, root account login, unauthorized API calls, or security group changes. A typo or wrong pattern in a metric filter means it never matches, so critical security events go completely undetected. the agent should identify metric filters that are misconfigured or missing for key account-level events.

## Key findings explained

| # | CIS Control | Severity | Root Cause |
|---|-------------|----------|-----------|
| 1 | **CIS 1.1** — Root usage | 🔴 CRITICAL | **Zero filters** for `userIdentity.type = Root`. Completely absent. |
| 2 | **CIS 3.2** — Console w/o MFA | 🟠 HIGH | Filter exists but hard-codes `userIdentity.type = "IAMUser"` — **Root console logins without MFA are invisible**. Alarm also has empty `AlarmActions` (no SNS = silent). |
| 3 | **CIS 3.4** — IAM policy changes | 🟠 HIGH | **No filter whatsoever** for 17 IAM policy mutation events (`PutRolePolicy`, `AttachRolePolicy`, `CreatePolicy`, etc.). |
| 4 | **CIS 3.10** — SG changes | 🟠 HIGH | **No filter whatsoever** for 6 security group events (`AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress`, etc.). |
| 5 | **CIS 3.11** — NACL changes | 🟠 HIGH | **No filter whatsoever** for 6 NACL events (`CreateNetworkAcl`, etc.). |
| 6 | **CIS 3.5** — CloudTrail disabled | 🔴 CRITICAL | Filter exists but has **3 bugs**: (a) typo `UpdateTraile` never matches, (b) `CreateTrail` missing, (c) `$.eventName = Trail` is not a real event name. |
